prediction.likelyOutcome: Montgomery Park is likely to prevail at the bench trial on the core question that the early termination was ineffective and the lease remained in force, and to recover the stated past-due rent (with NCO's overcharge/fraud/unjust enrichment claims facing a difficult, though not verified, path given typical fixed square-footage clauses in institutional leases). The far larger driver of total recovery -- rent for the ~46 months remaining on the term, plus contractual attorneys' fees and default-rate interest -- is very likely favorable to the landlord but cannot be quantified from the materials provided.

issues.label: Core liability: validity of early termination / lease continuation
Past-due rent as of the July 2011 default letter
Rent accrual for the remaining lease term (post-July 2011 through March 2015 expiration)
NCO's square-footage overcharge, unjust enrichment, and fraud claims
Attorneys' fees and costs under Section 14.04 fee-shifting clause

outcome.description: After a bench trial the district court entered judgment for Montgomery Park on its past-due-rent counterclaim of $9,854,566.95 plus postjudgment interest (upheld in earlier Fourth Circuit appeals at 842 F.3d 816, 918 F.3d 388 and 40 F.4th 123). The court then awarded $2,074,379.88 in attorneys' fees and nontaxable expenses, $115,942.10 taxable costs and $1,576,036.07 default interest ($3,766,358.05 total). In this fifth appeal the Fourth Circuit affirmed the fee/cost award (including expert fees) but vacated the default-interest component, holding interest runs only from the August 24, 2022 demand, and remanded for recalculation; the underlying rent judgment was not disturbed.
